title: Composing 'Lament for Javanette' at the Sherman Hotel
summary: He made up the tune alone on the bandstand in Chicago while girls dressed as Javanese sold cigarettes; Duke added an introduction and put his name on it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Like the Man from "Lament for Javonette". That's mine. Do you know how I did that?

At the Sherman Hotel in Chicago the girls used to dress like they were Javanese and they're selling cigarettes on the floor and the whole band is off, and I just sat up on the stage by myself on the bandstand and I just made up that little tune by myself. The next day we went to record it. Duke done put an introduction on it and fixed it up and dressed it up and put his name on it.
But did he keep the original name?
Because sometimes he would -- when he took something like that he would change the title.
No, he didn't change the title on that one. If there were any, he'd put his name on it. He'd put his name on to anything.
